claims.title: Unverified API authentication may let a customer-device caller reach internal order authority
claims.description: `flow:mobile-app-to-web-api:api-traffic` crosses from `boundary:customer-device` into `boundary:sokify-internal-systems` and terminates at `process:web-api`, but its `authentication` is unknown. If the API does not authenticate and authorize each incoming order request server-side, an anonymous attacker or a customer operating from the customer-device zone can invoke internal order-handling authority beyond their legitimate standing. This is conditional on the unresolved authentication and authorization behavior, not an assertion that it is absent. Second-order, `process:web-api` can hand accepted orders to `process:sims` through `flow:web-api-to-sims:order-handover` and maintains customer records, including financial and PII data, through `flow:web-api-to-user-database:customer-records`.

verdict.reason: The claim rests on `authentication` on `flow:mobile-app-to-web-api:api-traffic`, which the input never stated.

severity.justification: Likelihood is high conditional on the unknown authentication state: `crossing:flow:mobile-app-to-web-api:api-traffic` gives a customer-device position a path to `process:web-api`, and `unknown:flow:mobile-app-to-web-api:api-traffic:authentication` leaves credential verification unconfirmed. Impact is high because `process:web-api` handles `pii` and `financial` assets and reaches `store:user-database` over `flow:web-api-to-user-database:customer-records`.

mitigations.summary: Authenticate and authorize every API request at the receiving process
mitigations.detail: Make `process:web-api` validate a verified customer identity for `flow:mobile-app-to-web-api:api-traffic`, enforce server-side ownership and order permissions, and deny requests that lack a valid authorized subject.

mitigations.summary: Restrict internal order processing to authorized API actions
mitigations.detail: Ensure only validated, authorized order operations are forwarded over `flow:web-api-to-sims:order-handover`, rather than treating network arrival from the customer-device zone as authority.

claims.title: Forged customer API requests may be accepted if mobile-app authentication is absent
claims.description: `flow:mobile-app-to-web-api:api-traffic` crosses from the customer-device zone to `process:web-api` with `authentication: unknown`. If that attribute resolves to no verified caller identity, an attacker able to originate HTTP requests from outside Sokify can forge requests presented as `entity:customer` through `process:mobile-app`'s API channel, causing `process:web-api` to accept orders or customer-directed actions under the victim identity. Second-order: `process:web-api` reaches `store:user-database`, which holds customer name, address, and payment-card information, and hands placed orders to `process:sims`; this is conditional on the unknown authentication control, not an assertion that authentication is absent.

verdict.reason: The claim rests on `authentication` on `flow:mobile-app-to-web-api:api-traffic`, which the input never stated.

severity.justification: Likelihood is high, conditionally on the unknown authentication value: `flow:mobile-app-to-web-api:api-traffic` is a boundary crossing into internet-facing `process:web-api`, so an external attacker can attempt crafted requests. Impact is high because `process:web-api` is tagged `pii`, `financial`, and `business-critical-data`, and its downstream customer-record flow reaches `store:user-database` containing customer names, addresses, and payment-card information.

mitigations.summary: Establish and enforce verified customer authentication on the API flow
mitigations.detail: Record an explicit authentication mechanism for `flow:mobile-app-to-web-api:api-traffic` and require `process:web-api` to verify a customer-bound credential on every request rather than trusting caller-supplied identity.

mitigations.summary: Use short-lived, audience-bound customer tokens
mitigations.detail: Issue short-lived tokens bound to `process:web-api`, validate signature, expiry, audience, and subject on every request, and authorize actions against that verified subject.

claims.title: Flooding customer order traffic can exhaust the web API and halt order processing
claims.description: `process:web-api` is marked `internet-facing` and receives customer order-placement traffic from the customer-device zone over `flow:mobile-app-to-web-api:api-traffic`. If the `authentication` state on that flow does not enforce a verified caller before work is accepted, an attacker can cheaply flood the API with order-shaped requests while the API incurs customer-record work on `flow:web-api-to-user-database:customer-records` and forwards placed orders on `flow:web-api-to-sims:order-handover`. Resource limits, request-size limits, timeouts, and load shedding are not stated. Second-order, exhausting API workers, database capacity, or downstream handover capacity prevents legitimate customers from ordering and also blocks catalogue changes arriving on `flow:catalogue-spreadsheet-to-web-api:sql-statements`; this threat is conditional on the unresolved authentication/control posture, not an assertion that those controls are absent.

verdict.reason: The claim rests on `authentication` on `flow:mobile-app-to-web-api:api-traffic`, which the input never stated.

severity.justification: Likelihood is high, conditional on `unknown:flow:mobile-app-to-web-api:api-traffic:authentication`: customer traffic crosses from `boundary:customer-device` into `process:web-api`, which is marked `internet-facing`, so a remote attacker can repeatedly attempt requests with no stated prerequisite or metering control. Impact is medium: flooding `process:web-api` interrupts customer orders and the catalogue-update path, and propagates load toward the user database and SIMS, but no affected element is tagged `availability-critical` and the model describes a recoverable service outage.

mitigations.summary: Authenticate and meter order requests before downstream work
mitigations.detail: Require a verified caller before accepting expensive order paths on `process:web-api`, then apply per-identity and per-source rate and concurrent-request limits to `flow:mobile-app-to-web-api:api-traffic`.

mitigations.summary: Bound request and dependency consumption
mitigations.detail: Set hard request-size and parsing limits, worker/concurrency ceilings, and short timeouts for calls from `process:web-api` to the user database and SIMS; shed excess load early rather than queueing it into downstream order processing.

mitigations.summary: Isolate shared API workloads
mitigations.detail: Use separate bounded capacity or bulkheads for customer ordering and `flow:catalogue-spreadsheet-to-web-api:sql-statements` so a customer-facing flood cannot also prevent catalogue administration.

claims.title: A compromised marketing spreadsheet may borrow the Web API's broader database authority through raw SQL
claims.description: `process:catalogue-spreadsheet` in `boundary:marketing-office` sends SQL statements directly over `flow:catalogue-spreadsheet-to-web-api:sql-statements`, which crosses into `boundary:sokify-internal-systems`; authentication on that flow is unknown. If `process:web-api` executes or forwards those supplied statements without re-authorizing the originating marketing user and limiting them to an allowlisted catalogue operation, a party that compromises the marketing laptop can make the API exercise authority the party does not hold. This is an elevation through the API's standing access rather than merely the injection mechanism. Second-order, the API's authority reaches `store:user-database` via `flow:web-api-to-user-database:customer-records`, which holds customer names, addresses, and payment-card data, so unconstrained SQL execution could extend from catalogue changes to customer-record access or alteration.

An attacker positioned on the path between `process:mobile-app` and `process:web-api` can impersonate `process:web-api` to the mobile app, serving a look-alike endpoint and collecting or manipulating the customer details and order traffic the app sends. Second-order: a convincing fake API can induce `entity:customer` to submit information intended for the genuine ordering service, enabling subsequent misuse of that customer identity against the real API if credentials or session material are transmitted.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium: the flow crosses from the customer-device zone, but exploitation requires an attacker to gain an on-path position because transport encryption is stated absent. Impact is medium because the flow carries customer details and both `process:mobile-app` and `process:web-api` are tagged `pii`; successful endpoint impersonation can expose or solicit those details from customers.

mitigations.summary: Protect the mobile-app API channel with authenticated TLS
mitigations.detail: Change `flow:mobile-app-to-web-api:api-traffic` to HTTPS using TLS 1.2+ with full certificate-chain and hostname validation, so `process:mobile-app` verifies that it reached `process:web-api`.

mitigations.summary: Constrain API certificate issuance
mitigations.detail: Use an appropriately managed certificate identity for `process:web-api` and consider certificate pinning or a private service-identity scheme where operationally feasible to reduce look-alike endpoint acceptance.

claims.title: Forged spreadsheet-originated SQL may be accepted if API caller authentication is absent
claims.description: `flow:catalogue-spreadsheet-to-web-api:sql-statements` crosses from `boundary:marketing-office` into `boundary:sokify-internal-systems` with `authentication: unknown`. If `process:web-api` does not verify a distinct identity for `process:catalogue-spreadsheet`, an attacker with a foothold in the marketing-office zone can forge SQL submissions as the spreadsheet macros and have the API treat them as authorised catalogue updates. Second-order: the accepted statements can change prices and product copy handled by `process:web-api`, affecting the business-critical catalogue used by customer ordering. This draft is conditional on the unknown authentication attribute and does not claim that the API currently accepts unauthenticated SQL.

verdict.reason: The claim rests on `authentication` on `flow:catalogue-spreadsheet-to-web-api:sql-statements`, which the input never stated.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on the unknown authentication value: the flow crosses from `boundary:marketing-office`, so an attacker needs a foothold in that office zone, while the model provides no verified caller identity for the API to check. Impact is medium because the flow carries SQL statements that change prices and product copy, and both `process:catalogue-spreadsheet` and `process:web-api` handle `business-critical-data`.

mitigations.summary: Give the spreadsheet automation a distinct verified workload identity
mitigations.detail: Replace the unknown authentication on `flow:catalogue-spreadsheet-to-web-api:sql-statements` with a unique, short-lived service credential or mutually authenticated TLS identity that `process:web-api` verifies.

mitigations.summary: Limit the automation identity to catalogue operations
mitigations.detail: Authorize the verified spreadsheet identity only for narrowly defined catalogue-update operations rather than accepting arbitrary SQL statements, and rotate or revoke its credential independently of other workloads.

claims.title: On-path attackers can alter customer orders sent to the web API
claims.description: An attacker positioned between `process:mobile-app` in the customer-device zone and `process:web-api` can alter order-placement traffic on `flow:mobile-app-to-web-api:api-traffic`, which crosses into Sokify's internal systems with transport encryption explicitly absent. The attacker can change order details, including customer-provided details, before `process:web-api` processes them. Second-order, altered orders can be handed from `process:web-api` to `process:sims`, causing SIMS to act on corrupted order information and write or dispatch it onward.

grounds.text: Customers browse and order through our mobile app;
When an order is placed the API hands the order over to SIMS,

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium because exploiting the explicitly unencrypted boundary-crossing `flow:mobile-app-to-web-api:api-traffic` requires an on-path position; impact is medium because altered order data propagates to `process:sims` and affects business-critical fulfilment, but the model does not establish irreversible or broad financial compromise.

mitigations.summary: Protect mobile API traffic with authenticated TLS
mitigations.detail: Change `flow:mobile-app-to-web-api:api-traffic` from HTTP to HTTPS using TLS 1.2+ with certificate validation so an on-path party cannot modify requests undetected.

mitigations.summary: Validate order integrity at the API
mitigations.detail: Have `process:web-api` enforce server-side validation of order fields, prices, delivery details, and workflow transitions before forwarding an order to `process:sims`.

claims.title: Customer records can be directly rewritten if database write authentication is absent
claims.description: `flow:web-api-to-user-database:customer-records` is a read-write path into `store:user-database`, but its `authentication` attribute is unknown. If this unknown resolves to no effective caller authentication or authorization at the database write interface, an attacker who obtains network reachability to the store can alter customer names, addresses, or stored card-related records directly rather than through `process:web-api`. Second-order, `process:web-api` keeps and uses these customer records, so it can present or act on the attacker-modified values as authoritative application data. This is conditional on the unresolved authentication state of the database flow.

The web API keeps customers in the user database: name, address, and the card

verdict.reason: The claim rests on `authentication` on `flow:web-api-to-user-database:customer-records`, which the input never stated.

Impact is high because `store:user-database` holds customer names, addresses, and card-related data, is tagged `pii` and `financial`, and altered records are used by `process:web-api` as customer state.

mitigations.summary: Verify and enforce database caller authentication
mitigations.detail: Resolve the authentication design for `flow:web-api-to-user-database:customer-records` and require a dedicated workload identity for `process:web-api` before the database accepts writes.

mitigations.summary: Restrict database write privileges
mitigations.detail: Grant the web API identity only the tables and update operations it requires, enforce deny-by-default database policies, and separate read and write identities where feasible.

mitigations.summary: Detect and recover from unauthorized record changes
mitigations.detail: Add versioning, immutable change history, and reconciliation for sensitive customer-record updates so unauthorized rewrites can be identified and rolled back.
